what: Synthetic degradations of 8 holdout receipts the pipeline already reads well. NOT comparable to the CORD table; these numbers measure how much of a good read survives a named insult.
reading: Illumination flattening is a clear win on a clean shot, on a smooth lighting gradient and on thermal fade.

It is a LOSS on a hard-edged shadow, on a steep perspective and on blur. A box blur across a hard shade line leaves a halo; dividing by it over- and under-corrects either side of the edge, and the paper/table split then lands on the halo.

n=8 receipts and ~30 items, so each of those regressions is two or three items. The CORD evidence (120 real receipts across two disjoint slices, +12pp strict F1 on both) is far stronger, which is why flattening ships. The hard-shadow case is the next thing to attack, with an edge-preserving illumination estimate rather than a box blur.
